Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When a repo has a dedicated money helper module (e.g. ledgerly.money with round_money/to_money/ZERO), reuse those helpers for all monetary arithmetic and rounding instead of Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: For weighted-average computations, guard against division by zero by checking the total quantity/weight first and returning the project's ZERO constant for empty inputs.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Returning an unrounded Decimal from a money-returning function can fail hidden tests; apply the project's round_money to the final monetary result (e.g. weighted_total / total_quantity) before returning.

item.content: When validating an integer parameter, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since bool is a subclass of int and True/False would otherwise pass as 1/0.

Mirror the error codes and message formats used by sibling modules (e.g. payments.py's 'invalid_state' with f'invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}') so new validation paths stay consistent with the codebase's BillingError conventions.

Validating a raw unit_price before normalizing it can misclassify inputs; run it through the project's round_money/to_money first, then compare against ZERO, so float or string inputs are handled by the money helper rather than ad-hoc checks.
